subject: Post-event ROI & lead-credit: Hub Bites NYC — attendance + pipeline variance
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@gridly.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: events@gridly.com, tom@cornerstonehealth.com
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Hub Bites NYC — post-event attendance + leads (initial summary)

Hi Hannah / Marissa,

Thanks again for partnering with Gridly on Hub Bites in NYC last week — we had a strong turnout and several sponsor conversations that looked promising. Attached is the attendance summary and the raw lead dump from booth scans/check-ins. Please find quick highlights below: 

- Total registered: 642
- On-site checked in: 418
- Booth engagements (scans + meetings): 134
- Sponsor-claimed leads (Cornerstone Health): 28
- Organic booth leads (unclaimed): 38

We had two sources tied to the Cornerstone table: 1) sponsored digital registrations that were part of your promo code, and 2) organic walk-ups collected by the on-site team. The attached CSV includes a column "sponsor_claimed" where our ops team flagged which records Cornerstone asked to own at the time.

Questions we typically see after events: how many of the credited leads turned into HubSpot contacts with valid email + job title, and whether any leads were double-counted across sessions. If you can review the attached and confirm which rows you want credited to Cornerstone vs Redwood's marketing funnel, we can finalize the sponsor report and invoice.

Elena
Elena Park
Director, Events — Gridly
Gridly Events | events@gridly.com
Attachment: HubBites_NYC_attendance_summary.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB)
Attachment: sponsor_lead_dump_20260701.csv (csv, 105KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@gridly.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Hub Bites NYC — post-event attendance + leads (initial summary)

Elena — thanks for the quick summary and attachments. Appreciated. We pulled the CSV into our post-event pipeline model and have a few clarifying asks before we sign off: 

- Can you confirm the matching key you used for "sponsor_claimed"? We saw 7 records in the CSV flagged as Cornerstone-claimed that map to existing Redwood contacts (duplicate emails) — want to make sure we don’t double-credit.
- Do you have session-level source tags? A handful of the attendees were at the sponsored roundtable AND scanned the general booth; how do you prefer counting those?

Marissa / Ben — looping you in for the pipeline side. Marissa, could you run a quick dedupe on the CSV against HubSpot (contact dedupe + pql scoring) and flag any that have moved to MQL/SQL in the last 30 days? Ben, we might need to adjust sponsor credit if Cornerstone's contract included a closed-loop target (I think 20 qualified leads for a full credit).

Propose we do a 30-min call next week to align on final crediting and an invoice hold if needed.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Field Marketing Manager | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com

On Thu, 02 Jul 2026 at 09:14 Elena Park <elena@gridly.com> wrote:
> Hi Hannah / Marissa,
> 
> Thanks again for partnering with Gridly on Hub Bites in NYC last week — we had a strong turnout and several sponsor conversations that looked promising. Attached is the attendance summary and the raw lead dump from booth scans/check-ins...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Elena Park <elena@gridly.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 14:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Hub Bites NYC — post-event attendance + leads (initial summary)

Thanks Elena — dug into the CSV and compared against HubSpot (record view below). Quick notes and requests: 

- Dedupe: I removed 11 duplicates where the same email showed up as a session scan + a booth scan; after dedupe we have 123 unique booth engagements.
- Qualification: From those 123, 19 meet our 3-point PQL (title + company size + expressed interest). 11 of those were marked as Cornerstone-claimed by Gridly ops.
- Discrepancy: Cornerstone is showing 28 claimed leads on their internal tracker (Tom copied here) vs our 11 claim flags. We need a reconciliation because Contract SOW says credit=20 qualified leads for full sponsor activation discount.

Tom / Cornerstone — could you share the internal list you recorded at the event (emails or HubSpot ids) so we can match? I'll attach my exported HubSpot ids for the 19 PQLs.

Proposed approach to resolve quickly: 
1) Joint dedupe pass: Gridly exports original event id + scan timestamp; Cornerstone exports their claimed list; Redwood runs matching logic (email exact + phone normalization).
2) If matches < 20, we default to tiered credit: 0-9 => 25% credit, 10-19 => 50% credit, >=20 => 100% credit (per prior sponsor playbook).
3) Finalize numbers by Wed 07/08 so invoicing can reflect agreed credit.

Attaching: redwood_pql_export_20260706.csv (stub)

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Field Marketing Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood_pql_export_20260706.csv (csv, 28KB)

From: Tom Powell <tom@cornerstonehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena@gridly.com>, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Hub Bites NYC — post-event attendance + leads (initial summary)

Thanks all — quick note from Cornerstone's side: our on-site AE recorded 28 names/offers as sponsor leads (some handwritten notes). We uploaded those to our CRM overnight and I’m sharing our export here: Cornerstone_claimed_20260702.csv. We didn't sanitize for duplicates across sessions yet — that was my mistake. Happy to run matching with Marissa's export.

Ben / Hannah — if we land between 10-19 matched + qualified, Cornerstone will accept a 50% credit and a one-time promo code for a future event. If matched >=20, we accept full credit. If <10 matched we are requesting a 25% credit (per the playbook).

I'll make time for the call today if needed.

-Tom
Tom Powell
VP Partnerships | Cornerstone Health
Attachment: Cornerstone_claimed_20260702.csv (csv, 16KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Tom Powell <tom@cornerstonehealth.com>, Elena Park <elena@gridly.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 10:35:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Hub Bites NYC — post-event attendance + leads (initial summary) — reconciliation outcome

Quick reconciliation summary and actions (results of joint dedupe pass completed this morning):

- Raw Cornerstone list: 28
- Gridly sponsor_claimed flags in CSV: 11
- Redwood unique booth engagements after dedupe: 123
- Matched Cornerstone <-> Redwood (email exact + phone normalized): 16 matches
- Of those 16, 13 meet Redwood PQL criteria today (title + company size + expressed interest)

Agreed credit per sponsor playbook: matches = 16 => falls into 10-19 bracket => 50% credit. Cornerstone accepts the 50% credit + one-time promo code for a future event. We will: 

1) Apply 50% credit to sponsorship invoice (sponsorship-invoice-draft.pdf attached to the invoice record).
2) Send Cornerstone a promo code valid for next 12 months (Marketing to provide creative).
3) Redwood will add the 13 qualified leads to the Cornerstone lead view in HubSpot and tag them with "hub_bites_nyc_2026".
4) Gridly will update their sponsor report to mark 16 matched records and provide a short note for audit.

Next steps & owners: 
- Marissa: push the 13 qualified contacts to Cornerstone's CRM share (HubSpot) + add tags by EOD 7/8.
- Elena / Gridly: update their report and provide the event id mapping file to our ops (due 7/9).
- Hannah / Ben: approve final invoice adjustment and close the deal file (Ben to confirm updated invoice).

Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
Attachment: sponsorship-invoice-draft.pdf (pdf, 22KB)
